build_inputs.angles:
1. Lead on this: it was called the poor man's Ferrari, but the thing it was actually mocked for was the engine. The California T was the first turbocharged Ferrari road car since the F40 went out of production, and purists treated the twin-turbo V8 as Ferrari giving up the naturally aspirated scream to sell a cheaper car. 552 hp and roughly 557 lb-ft, in the model nobody took seriously.
2. Cover where Ferrari went next, because it changes what this car is. The mid-engine car is now a plug-in hybrid V6 - the 296 GTB, 819 hp, the first six-cylinder road car to wear the Ferrari badge, since the old Dino never did - and Ferrari has revealed its first electric car, the Luce. So the engine this car was punished for is the one people now want, and this is the cheap way into that V8.
3. For the head-to-head use the naturally aspirated Ferrari California it replaced - 4.3-litre V8, 453 hp, no turbos, the same folding hardtop 2+2 shape. The turbo car it was looked down on for is nearly 100 hp up on it.

title: 2015 Ferrari California T
youtube_title: From About $200,000 New to About $100,000 Today 🔥

history.fact: Ferrari launched the California T redesign in 2014, adding intercoolers beside the front grille for its turbocharged V8.

scenes.headline: $200K → $100K
scenes.narration: This one that cost about $200,000 new now goes for about $100,000. That's the 2015 Ferrari California T.

scenes.headline: Turbo Cooling
scenes.narration: Ferrari launched this redesign in 2014; intercoolers beside the grille feed its 553-horsepower V8.

scenes.headline: Carbon Ceramics
scenes.narration: Those wheels hide Brembo carbon-ceramic brakes, good for a claimed 112-foot stop from 62 mph.

scenes.headline: Muted Scream
scenes.narration: The 'poor man's Ferrari' lost its naturally aspirated scream; even equal-length headers couldn't satisfy purists.

scenes.headline: First Since F40
scenes.narration: Its twin-turbo 3.9-liter V8 makes 553 horsepower and 557 pound-feet; Ferrari hadn't turbocharged a road car since the F40.

scenes.headline: Seventh Gear
scenes.narration: That yellow tach monitors a flat-plane V8 whose full torque Ferrari only unlocks in seventh gear.

scenes.headline: Rear-Drive DCT
scenes.narration: Its seven-speed dual-clutch drives the rear wheels; Ferrari's F1-Trac reins in turbo torque exiting corners.

scenes.headline: Hybrid V6
scenes.narration: The mid-engined Ferrari 296 GTB pairs a plug-in hybrid V6 with 819 horsepower, Ferrari's first badge-wearing six-cylinder road car.

scenes.headline: Electric Future
scenes.narration: Ferrari's revealed the electric Luce too. Would you take this hundred-grand turbo V8 over its hybrid and electric future?

script: This one that cost about $200,000 new now goes for about $100,000. That's the 2015 Ferrari California T. Ferrari launched this redesign in 2014; intercoolers beside the grille feed its 553-horsepower V8. Those wheels hide Brembo carbon-ceramic brakes, good for a claimed 112-foot stop from 62 mph. The 'poor man's Ferrari' lost its naturally aspirated scream; even equal-length headers couldn't satisfy purists. Its twin-turbo 3.9-liter V8 makes 553 horsepower and 557 pound-feet; Ferrari hadn't turbocharged a road car since the F40. That yellow tach monitors a flat-plane V8 whose full torque Ferrari only unlocks in seventh gear. Its seven-speed dual-clutch drives the rear wheels; Ferrari's F1-Trac reins in turbo torque exiting corners. The mid-engined Ferrari 296 GTB pairs a plug-in hybrid V6 with 819 horsepower, Ferrari's first badge-wearing six-cylinder road car. Ferrari's revealed the electric Luce too. Would you take this hundred-grand turbo V8 over its hybrid and electric future?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2015 Ferrari California T, finished in Rosso Corsa with a black interior. The odometer currently displays approximately 17,000 miles. This California T is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes 20-inch wheels, carbon ceramic brakes, Scuderia Ferrari fender shields, a power-folding hardtop, leather upholstery, power-adjustable Daytona-style front seats, and carbon fiber interior trim. The seller reports no notable modifications. Service documentation in the gallery indicates that this California T had the transmission replaced in December 2025, at 14,215 miles. Designed by Pininfarina, the California made its debut for the 2009 model year as Ferrari's entry-level model. It was envisioned as a daily-drivable roadster, so it offered four seats and amenities not often associated with past models, such as a conventional navigation system. It was also Ferrari's first standard production model to feature a dual-clutch transmission, a power-folding hardtop, and a front-engine V8 configuration. The California T was introduced for the 2015 model year and featured a turbocharged power plant – the first in a Ferrari since the legendary F40. Power comes from a 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V8, rated at 553 horsepower and 557 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
